english: Let $S$ be the set of all ordered pairs $(a,b)$, where $a,b\in\{-10,-9,\ldots,9,10\}$, for which the function $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ defined by $f(x)=x^{3}+ax^{2}+bx$ is one-one. Then the number of elements in $S$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $S$ उन सभी क्रमित युग्मों $(a,b)$ का समुच्चय है, जहाँ $a,b\in\{-10,-9,\ldots,9,10\}$, जिनके लिए $f(x)=x^{3}+ax^{2}+bx$ द्वारा परिभाषित फलन $f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb{R}$ एकैकी है। तब $S$ में अवयवों की संख्या ______ है।
solution: $f$ is continuous on the interval $[0,\infty)$, so one-one $\Leftrightarrow$ strictly monotonic; as $f\to\infty$, it must be increasing: $f'(x)=3x^{2}+2ax+b\ge0$ on $[0,\infty)$ (zeros isolated).
$a\ge0$: vertex $-\frac a3\le0$, so the condition is $f'(0)=b\ge0$: $11\times11=121$ pairs.
$a<0$: vertex $-\frac a3>0$, condition $b\ge\frac{a^{2}}{3}$: $a=-1,-2,-3,-4,-5$ give $10,9,8,5,2$ values of $b$; $a\le-6$ gives none: $34$ pairs.
If $b<0$ or $b<\frac{a^2}{3}$ (as above), $f'<0$ near a point and $f$ decreases then increases, so it is not one-one.
solution_full: A continuous one-one function on an interval is strictly monotonic. Since $f(x)\to\infty$ as $x\to\infty$, a one-one $f$ on $[0,\infty)$ must be strictly increasing. Conversely, if $f'\ge0$ on $[0,\infty)$ with $f'$ vanishing only at isolated points, $f$ is strictly increasing and hence one-one.

So the condition is $f'(x)=3x^{2}+2ax+b\ge0$ for all $x\ge0$ (a quadratic that is not identically zero has isolated zeros). If $f'(x_{1})<0$ for some $x_{1}\ge0$, $f$ decreases near $x_{1}$ and later increases, so it takes some value twice and is not one-one.
The minimum of $f'$ on $[0,\infty)$: the vertex is at $x=-\dfrac a3$.
Case $a\ge0$: the vertex is at $x\le0$, so $f'$ is increasing on $[0,\infty)$ and the condition is $f'(0)=b\ge0$. With $a\in\{0,\ldots,10\}$ and $b\in\{0,\ldots,10\}$: $121$ pairs.
Case $a<0$: the vertex $-\dfrac a3>0$ and the minimum value is $b-\dfrac{a^{2}}{3}$, so the condition is $3b\ge a^{2}$ (equality gives $f'=3\left(x+\frac a3\right)^{2}$, still allowed).
originality_note: New: counting coefficient pairs for which a cubic is one-one on the half-line [0, infinity), where the condition splits by the position of the vertex of f' (way 5). Closest known: x^3 + ax^2 + bx + c increasing on R iff a^2 <= 3b. Different because: on the half-line the condition is b >= 0 for a >= 0 but a^2 <= 3b for a < 0, and the answer is a count with boundary cases.
blueprint_concepts: One-one vs many-one: monotonicity, horizontal line and algebraic tests

concept_use.Monotonicity in an interval: f' >= 0 on [0, infinity) split by the vertex -a/3 into b >= 0 or 3b >= a^2.
concept_use.One-one vs many-one: monotonicity, horiz: A continuous function on an interval is one-one iff strictly monotonic; a sign change of f' makes f many-one.

stem_review: Read as a student: every symbol, curve and function introduced with its domain; conditions complete; one reading of each sentence; answer unique and equal to the plan (positive 3-digit integer); Hindi mirrors the English maths. Range of a and b stated as integer lists; one-one on [0, infinity) only. No change.
key_step: One-one on the half-line means increasing there; the minimum of f' on [0, infinity) depends on the sign of a.
justification: Two ideas linked (one-one equals monotonic, monotonicity on a half-line with a vertex case split) followed by careful counting with boundary cases; comparable to the bounded counting anchor 2026-P1-Q11 (L3).
